correctness.rationale: Every square in a three-one word has zero or two ones. Zero-one-count squares are 0^(2k), and two-one-count squares have a unique root 0^x1 0^y whose two ones must occupy one of two adjacent pairs; inclusion-exclusion on the b=c diagonal yields the wordwise formula. Exact free-variable counting of these shapes yields the rational generating function as formal series. Pole extraction and weak-composition convergence yield the asymptotic mean and nondegenerate Dirichlet law. An independent substring-set scan checked all 31,465 three-one words of lengths 3 through 30 and 240 longer samples, and independent finite coefficient sums checked the generating function through zero-count 50. The finite checks are support, not replacements for the proofs.

evidence: Fraenkel–Simpson (1995), doi:10.37236/1196, proves an unavoidable/maximal-distinct-square problem for unrestricted binary sequences.
Deza–Franek–Thierry, arXiv:1310.3429, analyzes double-square structures and unrestricted upper bounds.
Brlek–Li, arXiv:2204.10204, gives a global alphabet-sensitive bound on distinct squares.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The global upper/maximum bounds do not specify the exact conditional square count for each three-one word nor sum its values over fixed-weight words. Those established statements are not stronger implication-wise than this complete conditional classification.

originality.rationale: The claimed object is the distinct set of literal contiguous squares conditional on exactly three one-symbols, not the unrestricted maximum, square-occurrence multiset, Abelian squares, or words with at most three squares. The zero-gap classification (1), complete aggregate generating function (2), and Dirichlet limit law (4) were not supplied by the materially inspected primary papers and accessible tables. A full 1998 article was inaccessible, so historical priority remains qualified; the core statements in accessible comparator works do not subsume the claim.
residual_risks: The full text of Fraenkel–Simpson (1998) was not accessible through available open sources or authorized institutional access; its detail-level overlap remains unverified.

value.rationale: Distinct literal square diversity is a standard and nontrivial invariant in combinatorics on words. Fixing exactly three one-markers makes a natural sparse family in which two differently placed adjacent marker pairs interact and require an overlap correction. The result gives an all-length exact wordwise classification, exact conditional aggregate generating function, sharp mean asymptotic, and nonconstant limiting law; these provide quantitative repetition profiles not implied by known unrestricted extremal bounds. The family is infinite and fully covered, not an arbitrary finite cutoff.
